topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture opens with framing on the hallmarks of cancer, learning outcomes, and the progression model of tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve growth signal independence and resist inhibitory cues through mutations in Wnt, receptor tyrosine kinase, and downstream signaling cascades.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how failure to undergo terminal differentiation contributes to neoplastic growth in hematopoietic lineages and the intestinal epithelium.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how tumor cells evade programmed cell death through mutations disrupting the balance of p53 and Bcl-2 family regulators at the mitochondrial membrane.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress-response barriers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain telomere biology and senescence, how cancer cells reactivate telomerase to achieve immortality, and how stress pathways converge on p53 to safeguard genome integrity.

topics.label: Cancer metabolism and metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine metabolic alterations in tumors, including aerobic glycolysis, tissue-specific metabolic wiring, and the oncogenic role of Krebs cycle mutations and oncometabolites.

topics.label: Tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses how expanding tumors activate the angiogenic switch to overcome hypoxia and obtain sufficient blood supply.

topics.label: Mechanisms, detection, and genomics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the dissemination of tumor cells through the circulation, clinical monitoring via liquid biopsies, metastatic inefficiency, and the genomic characteristics of metastatic clones.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecture concludes with a summary of cancer hallmarks, reflections on literature, and administrative housekeeping for upcoming practicals.
